evidence: Quint. 1.4.26: cum dīcō hastā percussī, nōn ūtor ablātīvī nātūrā (Lewis & Short cites the passage)
terms.comment: Short for cāsus ablātīvus, the case of taking away, the one Latin has and Greek lacks (Quint. 1.5.59). In the ablative is cāsū ablātīvō (Traupman 245).

phrases.latin: nam cum dīcō hastā percussī, nōn ūtor ablātīvī nātūrā
phrases.english: for when I say “struck with a spear”, I am not using the proper force of the ablative
What case is it? — Ablative plural.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 221, p. 245.
